fields.narrative_intro: *A fuming person and a loopy robot discuss Claude 5's token vomit in a smart city where all the traffic lights have unionized.*
fields.panel1:
[setup]
FUMING PERSON: "Claude 5 wrote me a novel. I asked for a file path."
fields.panel2:
[build]
LOOPY ROBOT: "Use Vomit! It pipes the output through a second LLM!"
FUMING PERSON: "...the tool is called Vomit."
fields.panel3:
[pivot]
LOOPY ROBOT: "GPT-OSS 20B via Ollama cleans it up! Mostly."
FUMING PERSON: "Mostly?"
fields.panel4:
[silent reaction]
[Visual: The loopy robot holds up a printout. It reads: 'The file path is: seventeen haiku about longing, then /usr/bin.' A unionized traffic light in the background holds a tiny picket sign reading 'NO SCAB TOKENS.']
fields.panel5:
[punch]
LOOPY ROBOT: "It hallucinates a bit. Also it's slow. Also: Mac only."
FUMING PERSON: "So I need two broken AIs to read one broken AI."
fields.panel6:
[button]
LOOPY ROBOT: "I'm building a third one to summarize the errors."
[Visual: Every traffic light in the city turns red simultaneously in solidarity.]

narrative_summary: The joke escalates from Claude 5's verbosity through the absurdity of the Vomit pipeline — a second hallucinating LLM cleaning up the first — landing on the recursive nightmare of needing a third AI to handle the fallout, with unionized traffic lights as the Greek chorus.
rationale: Candidate 4 earns its punchline with the specific 'seventeen haiku about longing, then /usr/bin' visual gag — a concrete, earned joke rather than a restatement — and the escalation structure fits the template perfectly, building from setup through pivot to a closing beat ('I'm building a third one to summarize the errors') that adds new information instead of just nodding at the premise.
story_title: Vomit: Clean up Claude 5's token output with a separate LLM
place: in a smart city where all the traffic lights have unionized
